column1: The school’s postal address is Hatfield, but it is actually nearer to Potters Bar, from which a £5 taxi ride takes one to the school.  Potters Bar is about 35 miles from Heathrow, about 45 – 50 minutes by taxi.

Taxi from Heathrow, or Airport Express to Paddington, and on to Potters Bar by Underground and mainline train.  This public transport journey is a bit complicated and girls apparently always choose to share cars.
Campus:
This is a rural school, set in the countryside about 2 miles from Potters Bar, but local buses are frequent and the school appeared to have a whole fleet of  mini-buses constantly running in and out.
Accommodation:

Boarding is organised by age-group – small shared bedrooms for the younger girls, moving to twin rooms and then singles further up the school.  It is all very modern and pleasant, with plenty of shared common-room space and good bathrooms.  50% of the 400 girls are boarders and flexi-boarders are also provided for, a great improvement on many girls’ schools these days, where boarding is very very small
Facilities:

This is a school which is clearly well-supported by a Foundation Fund!   The buildings and grounds appear very traditional, but inside everything is up-to-date and very well-kept.  Language labs, science labs, new theatre – everything is smart and clean.  Computer facilities are everywhere, the library has a good balance of books/computers.
General:
Examinations:    The school offers only A levels at present.
Uniform:
column2: A reasonably short uniform list.  Girls change into home clothes at the end of the school day and the uniform itself is realatively simple. Grey skirts and purple shirts and sweaters. Sixth Form girls wear their own clothes (smart jackets and skirts or trousers!)

column1: Admission:           Via the school’s own entrance tests
Suitable For:
Reasonably academic girls – feeder schools in Hong Kong include St Mary’s Canossian, Marymount and Maryknoll.  The atmosphere is very warm and very tolerant, so most girls would thrive here.
NOT Suitable For:
Girls only interested in work.
Girls who are very, very shy.  The school is very buzzy and a desperately shy girl might feel overwhelmed at times.
AA Comment:

It is nearly 20 years since I last visited Queenswood and it has transformed itself in that time! It is now a modern, lively school with a population of girls who are very polite, but extremely outgoing and lively."|""|""|""
Campus Location:

The school is 25 mins away from the nearest station – St Neots. The station is very small and there is a taxi station outside the train station. Regular service connects with St Neots and London King’s Cross station every day. It takes less than an hour to reach King’s Cross.
Campus:
The school is located in the village. The surroundings are residential areas.
The school will organise shuttle buses to send the boarders to Cambridge in weekends.
Accommodation:

There are 2 boarding houses which are located on the same street just opposite the school gate. Each boarding house has around 35 students. They are all share rooms from 2 to 4 persons. The rooms are quite spacious and they are clean and tidy. Bathrooms are newly refurbished. Students are allowed to go back to the boarding house for snacks during free time or lunch time. Relationships of the boarding housemasters and students are very close.
Facilities:
The school is about 190 acres, combined with modern and traditional buildings.

The main school is located in the Kimbolton Castle where the headmaster office located. The castle was mostly used for teaching as well. Students who studies humanities subjects are having their lessons inside the castle.

New science block is under construction and will be opened in September 2015. This includes 12 science laboratories and five new Maths classrooms (linking to three existing ones). It additionally houses a Digital Learning classroom, ICT server rooms, a greenhouse and technician areas.
Teaching are not only limited inside the classrooms but also the big grassland in the main campus. Different groups of students are having their lessons during the visit."|""|""|""
Campus Location:

Stephen Perse Sixth Form College is located near the City of Cambridge. It is about 20mins walk from the Cambridge station. Unlike the Junior and Senior School, the Sixth Form College is allocated separately on the other side of the Cambridge University Botanic Garden.
Campus:

The school is near the residential areas and the sports ground of the school. Most students live in town. Some activities or language lessons may be arranged in the Senior School after school, school will provide regular shuttle buses to transfer the students.
Accommodation:
Students have to arrange home stay on their own
Facilities:

School facilities are all very modern. The school has also rent another building as a new teaching block–The Shaftesbury Building which is just opposite the school main building. Conference rooms and school library has also been set up in the new building
Students can have lunch in the canteen and will be asked to pay for meals as taken.
Suitable For:
Students with good academic result
Independent student with good spoken English
NOT Suitable For:
Students who are shy and relying on others

The school is 15 miles away from London. There is a regular train service from Victoria and Waterloo to Epsom. Epsom is located on the slopes of Epsom Downs in Surrey, which is 10 mins from Epsom Station.
Campus:

The campus is around 85 acres. Teaching blocks are concentrated with each other while most of the boarding houses are allocated on the other side of the campus. The campus is very well-organised, grouping with different sectors and departments.
Accommodation:

There are 8 boarding houses including 5 boys’ boarding houses and 3 girls’ boarding houses. Boarding is organised by vertical system except the White House - Boarding house for sixth form girls. Most of the boys’ boarding houses are newly refurbished. Students are sharing in to twin rooms and then singles further up the school.  It is all very modern and pleasant, with plenty of shared common-room space and good bathrooms. Students are welcome to go back to the boarding house anytime during day time.
Facilities:

The school buildings and grounds appear very traditional, but inside everything is up-to-date and very well-kept. Everything is smart and clean. Facilities are very nice including indoor swimming pool, gymnastic room, CCF training site etc. The School Shop is really big. Students can nearly purchase all essential things inside the shop.
Suitable For:
Students who are looking for school with many activities and like to do sports.
NOT Suitable For:
Students who only interested in work.

Dean Close School is located in Gloucestershire. The nearest train station is Cheltenham Spa which is around 5 mins taxi ride or 10 mins walk from the school. There are several direct trains each day from London Paddington Station and the journey is about 2hr long.
Campus:

The School is divided into pre-prep, preparatory and senior schools located on separate but adjacent sites outside Cheltenham town centre. Most of the school buildings are enclosed with each other while the Sports Center and the School Shop is on the other side of the school site.
Accommodation:

There are 3 girls’ and 3 boys’ boarding houses. They are organised in vertical system. Two of the boarding houses are for sixth formers only. I’ve visited one of the girls’ boarding house – Shelburne. It is a building with four floors. It is very close to the rugby pitch, near the exit of the school. The interior of the house is very modern and girlish style. There is a long corridor for each floor with around 20 rooms on each floor. Walls are painted in yellow, orange and pink colour for each room. Most of the girls are sharing in 4 beds in a room. The 4th form and 5th form girls will be sharing in triple or twin beds in a room. Upper sixth students can be arranged for a single room. The rooms are spacious and tidy. There is a lift inside the house. Suitcases can be kept inside the room. Another boys’ boarding - Brook Court House is located near the Music School of the school. It is a building with 2 floors only with traditional boarding house settings. Students are allowed to come back during break and lunch time. Relationships of students and the boarding housemaster are quite close.
Facilities:

The facilities of the school are quite modern. The school especially focuses their resources on Drama and Art. There are 10 drama productions every year on average, from whole school musicals to pupil-produced plays.
Suitable For:
Girls who want good pastoral care with modern facilities of the school
Not Suitable For:
Girls who want to join traditional school
AA Comment:

The interior design and setting of the boarding house are very nice. The school is very concern about the pastoral care and guardian issue of students. In order to help the new students to settle down well, induction week will be arranged at the beginning for September. Most of the interior design of the schools is very modern."|""|""|""

- Government School
- Tuition fee (only) at about GBP 9,500 per annum
- In a small town within New Forest National Park (Very safe)
- 15 mins to the closest city, 90 mins to central London
- Class size: 17-22 per class
- Chinese students: 20 from mainland, 5 from HK
- Aim: Build an international learning environment, school against big group of single nationality
- To apply: UKVI Test at approved centre / IELTS Centre (Should have more than 5.0 in each test)
Also need to submit: 1.) Personal statement + 2.) Copy of passport + 3.) Academic Reports from the past 2 yrs
- Extracirricular activies: Twice a week (Optional but encouraged)
Courses and Exams:
- Offers A-levels and Foundation courses
- For A-Levels: Need to do 3 subjects minimum not including Chinese (And for gifted students: can do extra EPQ)
- Chinese A-Levels in Mandarin
- For Foundation: Collaborate with universities like Reading and Bournemouth etc. 100% progression rate (guaranteed)

- Foundation at Brock's advantage over uni: Cheaper (GBP 19,000), pro-active extra support for students, more flexible (students can choose to apply which uni and change their minds), UCAS guidance provided within college.
- STEP and AEA exams available especially for Oxbridge Maths applicants
- Free Aspire tests
- 47 GCSEs subjects available (66% got A* to B grades) *Unlikely, need to recheck*
Host Families:
- All from local areas
- School directly in charge of and responsible for host arrangement and selection (not outsourced)
- High satisfaction rate from students (>85%)
- 2 meals (breakfast and dinner) provided during weekdays. Recommend students to bring GBP 5 for lunch.
- 3 meals provided on holidays
- Rates/price depends on commuting time (NOT distances)
- Price range: GBP 6,600-7,500 (Price INCLUDES travel pass)
- Accommodation on first-come-first-serve basis
- No extra guardian required for students"|"MURPHY Melissa"|""|""
Campus Location:
The nearest station of the school is Godalming. It is about less than an hour to London Waterloo.
Campus

The campus is located on the slope. The school occupies a large site in excess of 200 acres. The original neo-Gothic school building comprises the four ‘old houses’, while the eight ‘new houses’ were.
Accommodation:

Students are divided amongst the twelve boarding Houses. The original three – Saunderites, Verites and Gownboys (where scholar lives and entitled to wear gown), known as the Block Houses, together with one other, Girdlestoneites – are grouped at the centre of the School and are collectively known as the ‘Old’ Houses. Seven Houses – Lockites, Weekites, Hodgsonites, Daviesites, Bodeites, Pageites and Robinites are called the ‘New’ Houses.

A sixth form House, Fletcherites, is opened in 2010. Fletcherites is a mixed boarding House for sixth formers only and all the First Year Specialists (Year 12) in this House are new to the School. The boys and girls have shared common rooms and other facilities, with separate residential accommodation.

The other eleven Houses have sixth form year groups of approximately two thirds boys and one third girls. The girls spend the working day as an integral part of their House and return to their Halls of Residence at the end of the evening
Students have their lunch and dinner at school in the central dining hall.
Facilities:

The sporting facilities are impressive and include: the Queen's Sports Centre; athletics track; three all weather Astro pitches; flood lit tennis courts; fives, racquets and squash courts; and The Halford Hewitt Golf Course. The Halford Hewitt Golf Course is a 9-hole, par 34 course occupying approximately 30 acres of the Charterhouse campus. The Queen's Sports Centre has an indoor swimming pool, multi-use sports hall, climbing wall and a well-equipped fitness gym. Art Center and Music block are very outstanding as well. Pupils regularly perform in ten minute recitals during quarter (the morning break), and there is a host of choirs and ensembles: Chapel Choir, Chamber Choir, Symphony Orchestra, String Orchestra, Jazz Band and Brass Ensemble and Concert Band. School Shop and School Library are huge. Students can visit the library anytime and opened till night time."|""|""|""

Shrewsbury School is situated in Shrophire, to the northwest of Birmingham. As there is no direct train service to this location, one has to change train in Birmingham in order to get there. The train journey takes about 2 hours 45 mins. To reach the toun centre, however a 10 mins walk is required from Shrewsbury train station, whereas a 15 mins ride by taxi is needed in order to get from Shrewsbury train station to the institute.
Campus
-150 acres, red bricked buildings, lots of greens
Accommodation

A total of 9 boarding houses and 2 day houses can be found within the school campus. I was taken on a tour to the “School House” right next to the main school. The boarding house system is described as a vertical one which implies that one can find all year groups boarders under the same roof.
The school house can accommodate a total of 84 boarders spreading over a building 5 storeys high.

For lower form boarders, they can share a room with a minimum of two and a maximum of 5 occupants. No desk can be found in the room however to ensure that studying activities are confined to the study room. In order words, the sleeping room sole purpose is only meant for resting.
The 6th formers, nonetheless, are entitled to have the privileges of staying alone in single rooms of their own. They enjoy more privacy.

I was also shown to a place called” Emma Darwin Hall” which incidentally is a boarding house for girls. Everything there was nice, brand new and modern. Here, one can enjoy the convenience of having desks to work and above all, elevators for climbing staircases instead.
Facilities
- The resourceful library is well-stocked with materials of all kinds of tranquil and cosy environment make one feels like reading at home.
- The Economics and Science building is a newly completed classroom block which looks a bit more modern in comparison to the order surrounding building complex.

- Sport is highly valued here in Shrewsbury School. Football is the most popular sport pursued by the majority of the students who find it most enjoyable with the numerous up-dated facilities available.
Rowing has become a big sport here at Shrewsbury School too. The rowing teams here as can be expected, quite sizable in nature.
Other sports like Rugby, netball, fencing, badminton, basketball, rickets, and hockey also constitute part of the regular school curriculum.
There is also an indoor swimming pool and a gym to cater for the needs of those who care to shape –up their bodies.
-A new design and technology centre was opened in September 2016 within the school campus. The building is new and modern with plenty of pupils’ works. Good DT!
-In addition, a new academic hall has recently been put into service as well. (just opened in 2015)
-Standard of Art is really impressive. Exhibits of the pupils’ Art works are displayed for appreciation.
-The school chapel is well-decorated with tinted-glasses, which makes the whole place look solemn yet colourful.
-Pupils have their meals at a central dining hall. (I had my lunch there, foods-wide range, taste ok…)
- School will provide coach service for international students with small fees from Heathrow to Shrewsbury School on the first day/last day of term.
General

column1: Campus Location

Covering a total area of over 350 acres, RMS is located within easy access from the heart of London City. It is well-connected by the tube system. To get there, one can get on a faster train which runs from Marylebone to Rickmansworth in 20 mins. The school is then a short walk of 10-15 mins from the train station.
Apart from its ease of accessibility, the historical school premises offer a unique landscape design and tranquil environment conducive to a perfect learning atmosphere.
Campus

The layout of the campus is rather unique and beautifully design. The boarding house and the prep department are arranged in a perfect semi-circle. The two ends are linked up by the main building of classrooms, In fact, it is only here that one can expect to find the longest classroom corridor in the whole of Europe, rather unusual but impressive!
Green areas can be found almost everywhere around the campus.
Chapel is impressive! Interestingly, one student whom I talked to told me that a number of teachers had actually held their wedding ceremonies in the school chapel!
Accommodation
The 5 boarding houses currently operating provided fully-furnished yet spacious bedrooms to all boarding pupils who desire a cosy living condition.
Starting from Sept 2016 onwards, however, the 5 boarding houses will be re-organized into 3 categories instead.
Pupils in Year9 and 10 will share a room with room-mates 2 to 3. Those in Year 11, with 1-2, whereas Year 12 pupils will have the advantage of staying in a single room on their own.

To make living less monotonous, however rooms swapping would be implemented at the end of each school-term. It should be emphasized that in order to cultivate their independency as well as more enjoyable, Year 13 pupils are entitled to have access to a bigger kitchen which enable them to prepare their own foods on their own, hence, they might choose not to have their meals at the dining hall.
Facilities

A well-equipped sports centre is established which offers all-round gymnastic-trainings. In essence the institute has been renowned for its outstanding gymnastic team for decades. Other popular facilities found include bicycle-tracks, squash counts and an indoor swimming pool. In addition, for tennis enthusiasts, a total of 14 tennis courts is available. Last but not least, one other special feature is the presence of a modern dance studio.
Instead of the commonly used long-tables, round ones have been used instead which make the setting seen more like a “high school musical”!
I enjoyed my lunch provided by the school canteen together with several other RMS pupils during the visit and they unanimously told me that they really liked the food served there!
General
-Art & textile, history and Geo are popular in GCSE
-RMS offer 32 subjects at AL
-Geo is very popular in AL
-GCSE class size –max. 18

The campus is around 85 acres. Teaching blocks are concentrated with each other while most of the boarding houses are allocated on the other side of the campus. The campus is very well-organised, grouping with different sectors and departments.
Accommodation:

There are 8 boarding houses including 5 boys’ boarding houses and 3 girls’ boarding houses. Boarding is organised by vertical system except the White House - Boarding house for sixth form girls. Students who are looking for school with many activities and like to do sports. They do different sports every term.

Students who only interested in work.

The school’s postal address is Hatfield, but it is actually nearer to Potters Bar, from which a £5 taxi ride takes one to the school.  Potters Bar is about 35 miles from Heathrow, about 45 – 50 minutes by taxi.

Taxi from Heathrow, or Airport Express to Paddington, and on to Potters Bar by Underground and mainline train.  This public transport journey is a bit complicated and girls apparently always choose to share cars.
Campus:
This is a rural school, set in the countryside about 2 miles from Potters Bar, but local buses are frequent and the school appeared to have a whole fleet of  mini-buses constantly running in and out.
Accommodation:

Boarding is organised by age-group – small shared bedrooms for the younger girls, moving to twin rooms and then singles further up the school.  It is all very modern and pleasant, with plenty of shared common-room space and good bathrooms.  50% of the 400 girls are boarders and flexi-boarders are also provided for, a great improvement on many girls’ schools these days, where boarding is very very small
Facilities:

This is a school which is clearly well-supported by a Foundation Fund!   The buildings and grounds appear very traditional, but inside everything is up-to-date and very well-kept.  Language labs, science labs, new theatre – everything is smart and clean.  Computer facilities are everywhere, the library has a good balance of books/computers.
General:
Examinations:    The school offers only A levels at present.
Uniform:
column2: A reasonably short uniform list.  Girls change into home clothes at the end of the school day and the uniform itself is realatively simple. Grey skirts and purple shirts and sweaters. Sixth Form girls wear their own clothes (smart jackets and skirts or trousers!)

Shrewsbury School is situated in Shrophire, to the northwest of Birmingham. As there is no direct train service to this location, one has to change train in Birmingham in order to get there. The train journey takes about 2 hours 45 mins. To reach the toun centre, however a 10 mins walk is required from Shrewsbury train station, whereas a 15 mins ride by taxi is needed in order to get from Shrewsbury train station to the institute.
Campus
-150 acres, red bricked buildings, lots of greens
Accommodation

A total of 9 boarding houses and 2 day houses can be found within the school campus. I was taken on a tour to the “School House” right next to the main school. The boarding house system is described as a vertical one which implies that one can find all year groups boarders under the same roof.
The school house can accommodate a total of 84 boarders spreading over a building 5 storeys high.

For lower form boarders, they can share a room with a minimum of two and a maximum of 5 occupants. No desk can be found in the room however to ensure that studying activities are confined to the study room. In order words, the sleeping room sole purpose is only meant for resting.
The 6th formers, nonetheless, are entitled to have the privileges of staying alone in single rooms of their own. They enjoy more privacy.

I was also shown to a place called” Emma Darwin Hall” which incidentally is a boarding house for girls. Everything there was nice, brand new and modern. Here, one can enjoy the convenience of having desks to work and above all, elevators for climbing staircases instead.
Facilities
- The resourceful library is well-stocked with materials of all kinds of tranquil and cosy environment make one feels like reading at home.
- The Economics and Science building is a newly completed classroom block which looks a bit more modern in comparison to the order surrounding building complex.

- Sport is highly valued here in Shrewsbury School. Football is the most popular sport pursued by the majority of the students who find it most enjoyable with the numerous up-dated facilities available.
Rowing has become a big sport here at Shrewsbury School too. The rowing teams here as can be expected, quite sizable in nature.
Other sports like Rugby, netball, fencing, badminton, basketball, rickets, and hockey also constitute part of the regular school curriculum.
There is also an indoor swimming pool and a gym to cater for the needs of those who care to shape –up their bodies.
-A new design and technology centre was opened in September 2016 within the school campus. The building is new and modern with plenty of pupils’ works. Good DT!
-In addition, a new academic hall has recently been put into service as well. (just opened in 2015)
-Standard of Art is really impressive. Exhibits of the pupils’ Art works are displayed for appreciation.
-The school chapel is well-decorated with tinted-glasses, which makes the whole place look solemn yet colourful.
-Pupils have their meals at a central dining hall. (I had my lunch there, foods-wide range, taste ok…)
- School will provide coach service for international students with small fees from Heathrow to Shrewsbury School on the first day/last day of term.
General

column2: If students want to apply for sport scholarship, need to fly to the UK to do fitness test+ test 2 sports

6th formers can choose their tutor by their own tutor by their own, good relationship between tutors and students ie they go cinema, students will go to tutor’s house to sleepover, they meet at least 3-4 times a week
Big subjects at Shrewsbury: Maths, Bio, Chem, Physics, Econ, Eng, History"|""|""|""

column1: Campus Location

Covering a total area of over 350 acres, RMS is located within easy access from the heart of London City. It is well-connected by the tube system. To get there, one can get on a faster train which runs from Marylebone to Rickmansworth in 20 mins. The school is then a short walk of 10-15 mins from the train station.
Apart from its ease of accessibility, the historical school premises offer a unique landscape design and tranquil environment conducive to a perfect learning atmosphere.
Campus

The layout of the campus is rather unique and beautifully design. The boarding house and the prep department are arranged in a perfect semi-circle. The two ends are linked up by the main building of classrooms, In fact, it is only here that one can expect to find the longest classroom corridor in the whole of Europe, rather unusual but impressive!
Green areas can be found almost everywhere around the campus.
Chapel is impressive! Interestingly, one student whom I talked to told me that a number of teachers had actually held their wedding ceremonies in the school chapel!
Accommodation
The 5 boarding houses currently operating provided fully-furnished yet spacious bedrooms to all boarding pupils who desire a cosy living condition.
Starting from Sept 2016 onwards, however, the 5 boarding houses will be re-organized into 3 categories instead.
Pupils in Year9 and 10 will share a room with room-mates 2 to 3. Those in Year 11, with 1-2, whereas Year 12 pupils will have the advantage of staying in a single room on their own.

To make living less monotonous, however rooms swapping would be implemented at the end of each school-term. It should be emphasized that in order to cultivate their independency as well as more enjoyable, Year 13 pupils are entitled to have access to a bigger kitchen which enable them to prepare their own foods on their own, hence, they might choose not to have their meals at the dining hall.
Facilities

A well-equipped sports centre is established which offers all-round gymnastic-trainings. In essence the institute has been renowned for its outstanding gymnastic team for decades. Other popular facilities found include bicycle-tracks, squash counts and an indoor swimming pool. In addition, for tennis enthusiasts, a total of 14 tennis courts is available. Last but not least, one other special feature is the presence of a modern dance studio.
Instead of the commonly used long-tables, round ones have been used instead which make the setting seen more like a “high school musical”!
I enjoyed my lunch provided by the school canteen together with several other RMS pupils during the visit and they unanimously told me that they really liked the food served there!
General
-Art & textile, history and Geo are popular in GCSE
-RMS offer 32 subjects at AL
-Geo is very popular in AL
-GCSE class size –max. 18

column1: 197|"20160429"|"20180322180159"|"AA00042"|"Godolphin School is one of the oldest girls’s boarding school in the UK (the school is ard 300 year-old!) The school is located on a hill to the east of the city of Salisbury with a lovely view of the cathedral. It is a town school. It is about 1.5 hours from London to Salisbury by train and just a 5-10 mins walk from Salisbury town centre.
Godolphin has one junior boarding house (7-12 years) and two senior boarding houses (13-16 years).
-normally 4-6 girls share a big bedroom

Sixth form centre comprises 2 boarding houses with common rooms, kitchens and relaxation areas. Houses accommodate both Upper and lower Sixth boarders and also day girls. There is a range of single and double study bedrooms for the boarders and each day girl has her own individual work area in the Centre. The school ensures that all the girls are fully integrated.

Each sixth former belongs to the same small tutor group for both her lower and upper sixth year so that her tutor can get to know her well and can guide her in her academic work and oversee her progress.

-There is no central dining room- even day girls will allocate to a houses and everyone who belongs to the house eats all meals there (I was told by a 6th form HK student that the food at Godolphin is excellent, especially the breakfast! They have Green Monday as well)
-6th formers can choose to have single or share bedrooms
-all rooms are bright and bathrooms are clean
-boarding facilities provide a warm environment in which the girls can work, relax and socialise
-all boarders benefit from an extensive programme of activates for everyday of the week and weekend
Facilities

The playing fields are on-site however the sport hall is off-campus. I haven’t visit the sport hall but was told that it is easily accessible. Girls can join regular yoga, fitness and relaxation session held in the Sixth form Centre. There are many sporting options available at Godolphin: netball, hockey cross-country, swimming, tennis, cricket, fencing, basketball, volleyball etc.
The Sixth form centre included facilities such as IT suites, conference room, relaxation suites and a Sixth Form Centre Café which they serve Costa drinks.
Art has a huge and impressive building bursting with stunning work.
There are so many opportunities to lean different things and to be ready for whatever you want to do after school.
All of the girls and staff at the school belong to one of three houses. These houses come together for competitive purposes in activities ranging from debating, drama to sport."|""|""|""
Dauntsey’s School is situated in the village of Wiltshire.
Nearby station is Westbury (25 mins away from the school). There is a direct train from Westbury to London Paddington. It takes around 1.5 hours.
Accommodation
There are 5 boarding houses and 7 day houses.
Lower school houses- 3 day houses,1 boarding houses-Manor (off-campus)
Upper school houses-2 day houses and 2 boarding houses for Boys, 2 day houses and 2 boarding houses for Girls
Every pupil joins either a boarding or day house, which are co-educational in the Lower School (ages11-13) and single sex in the Upper school (ages 14-18).

The Manor is co-educational house. The boys and girls accommodation is on separate floors. It is a fabulous Victorian mansion set in 65 acres of grounds and ancient woodland. The house can accommodate approx. 70 lower school boarders. It is a very caring and friendly “home from home” atmosphere. As well as a large array of indoor leisure facilities, outside there are tennis courts, a seven-hole golf course. Boarders will have many activities and competitions in the Manor grounds.
Boarders will have breakfast and supper here and then walk with a group of 3 or take mini bus to the school.
Fitzmaurice (Upper school boarding, Boys 14-18 years)
Fitzmaurice is one of the two boys’ upper school boarding house at Dauntsey’s. The house accommodates around 60 boys, with each sixth former having his own room.
For lower form boarders, they shared a room with 2-4.
Evans (Upper School boarding, Girls 14-18 years)
The house has 36 single room and 12 double rooms is of high quality. Sixth formers can have ensuite bedroom. The rooms are bright and spacious. For lower form boarders, they shared a room with 2-4.

Each house is run by a housemaster or housemistress and a team of tutors who take a close and active interest in pupils’ academic and social development, as well as encouraging them to make the most of the activities on offer. A student team in each house organises a range of activities and event throughout the year. There’s always something going on, from outdoor movie nights, themed parties, high teas, trips to the theatre, bowling etc.

Boarders and day pupils are fully integrated. Day pupils also benefit from the many events and opportunities on offer beyond the school day to which they are always welcome. Boarders often make friends with local day pupils, and are able to invite them to stay at no cost, in their boarding house at the weekend.
Facilities

-Sport plays an important role in the school and pupils are expected and encouraged to take an active part. Sporting opportunities are everywhere. Major sports include basketball, football, cricket, hockey, netball, rugby and tennis.
Excellent sport facilities including 8 rugby/football pitches,2 hockey pitches, 7netball/tennis courts, a huge sport hall, heated swimming pool, 2 squash courts
-Tuck shop. Pupils can buy snacks, drinks. Cyber Café is next door, pupils keen to catch up with friends here and test the latest and hottest in computer games!
-Dining. There are always choices of two hot courses, with a vegetarian option available. Daily Salad bar offers many options! Homemade soups, hot and cold dessert, fresh fruit, yogurt etc…

-Good Art department. There is the exhibition area in the central of the Art block which hosts a wide range of pupils and guest artist’s works. Art teacher is very supportive. I can see it’s a stimulating and encouraging environment to work in.
-Music is equally strong at Dauntsey’s. Around 400 pupils taking lessons in 20 different instruments. Pupils are participating in many concerts, competitions and master classes.
-6 to7 drama productions every year and a major dance showcase, there is plenty of opportunity offer to pupils studying at Dauntsey’s
General

School uniform is worn by all pupils from the first to the fifth form. Sixth form pupils can wear smart casual. They are not expected to wear school uniform but their dress and appearance should be in a style that would be appropriate in a formal business environment.
-16 pupils in GCSE class
-Max. 12 pupils in AL class
- EAL is included"|""|""|""

column1: Just thought I would send you a summary of my visit to Sedbergh School yesterday.  It is actually 10 years since I was last at the school and it was good to meet up with a few familiar faces.  David Milner, the Director of Marketing & Admissions , met me when I arrived and I then had a meeting with the Deputy Head, Dr Jenny Burns, who joined the school in 2021 from Durham School.  The Headmaster sent his best wishes and was sorry he wouldn’t see me but he was in London at a fundraising event.

Two Hong Kong pupils accompanied me on a tour of the school.  Fione and Isaac are both 14 years old and joined the school last year in Year 9.  Fione is a little quiet but a very nice girl and she particularly enjoys her Art and Design - told me she would probably stay for the Sixth Form and she seems happy and settled.  Isaac seemed a bit more ambitious and very confident – he said his mother is a Barrister and his father a Specialist Surgeon – he said he would probably go on to another more academic school for the Sixth Form which was interesting.  Fione’s three words to sum up the school were:  Family/Sporty/Tiring and Isaac’s were:  Family/Care/Sympathy.  Good to see that they both said Family and I do think this could partly be because the school has retained the house dining system – there are only five schools left with this system in the UK as it is much more expensive than having central feeding.  I do feel it does, however, create a family atmosphere when you have all your meals in your boarding house.

It was raining quite heavy during my tour and I did not see as much as I would have liked.  The sports facilities are very good and the Hurst Centre that was opened three years ago has a multi-functional sports hall that converts for formal occasions and has seating for 1,000 – it also houses a fitness centre and very nice hospitality facilities.  The next major development is a Design/Computing and Technology Centre which will be built for September 2025.  The main school building has been refurbished and there is a very nice entrance and reception area for visitors.  The general classroom areas that I visited remain very much the same.  I only visited the communal areas of one of the boys houses which has had some refurbishment but did not see any bedrooms.  I had lunch on one of the girls houses and the food was good – I did ask to see some of the girls bedrooms and they are fine but I did think they were particularly messy and untidy.  I have read the Inspection Report from February this year and the school meets all the necessary regulations but interestingly states that the boarding accommodation is “adequate”.  I did speak to David Milner about this when I met him for coffee before I left.  I told him that I had recommended the refurbishment of the boys houses 10 years ago – he said that work was very much ongoing but with such large properties that were constantly in use it was a long process.  I asked him to send me some images as I had not seen any of the rooms during my tour.

The school is doing well and the boarding houses are full – they have been granted an increase in their numbers for next year.  I really did not see any other pupils from China as I toured the school and Fione and Isaac are the only ones from Asia on their houses.  I feel that the main reason for this, especially for the market, is that Sedbergh is still not recognised as an academic school and pupils really do need to want to embrace sport and outdoor life as part of their education.  I did discuss this with David and he fully understands.  The positive is that at the weekends the school remains full and very busy – they have refused to go down the flexi/weekly boarding route and it does seem to have paid off.  Out of 550 pupils, they only have 20 day pupils and they are the children of staff and some local scholars from the State schools in the area.

Sedbergh would really like to be part of the next physical  AA event and they have built up a good reputation for their sport in HK.   I said I would pass on this message to you and they said they would be thrilled if they were invited.  For HK families with very bright, studious children Sedbergh is not an option.  If there are families, however, with children who enjoy their sport and the outdoors and are average academically then they would certainly be getting a British boarding school experience and plenty of fresh air!!  Interesting to note that Fione said her parents chose Sedbergh so she would have the opportunity to be much more active than she had been in HK and she would be more healthy.  Isaac also said that he thought he was a bit of a wimp before joining Sedbergh and he now felt more resilient after being so active!

In summary, Sedbergh is a very busy bustling school but I still maintain that it is best suited to students who have quite strong personalities and who enjoy being very active.  I think it is quite a hard environment and more gentle students might struggle with the rough and tumble.  The housemistress that I had lunch with was going wild water swimming in the afternoon (in November!!) with pupils – I rest my case!!!!!!!!"|""|""|""

column1: - Tuition fee (only) at about GBP 9,500 per annum
- In a small town within New Forest National Park (Very safe)
- 15 mins to the closest city, 90 mins to central London
- Class size: 17-22 per class
- Chinese students: 20 from mainland, 5 from HK
- Aim: Build an international learning environment, school against big group of single nationality
- To apply: UKVI Test at approved centre / IELTS Centre (Should have more than 5.0 in each test)
Also need to submit: 1.) Personal statement + 2.) Copy of passport + 3.) Academic Reports from the past 2 yrs
- Extracirricular activies: Twice a week (Optional but encouraged)
Courses and Exams:
- Offers A-levels and Foundation courses
- For A-Levels: Need to do 3 subjects minimum not including Chinese (And for gifted students: can do extra EPQ)
- Chinese A-Levels in Mandarin
- For Foundation: Collaborate with universities like Reading and Bournemouth etc. 100% progression rate (guaranteed)

- Foundation at Brock's advanage over uni: Cheaper (GBP 19,000), pro-active extra support for students, more flexible (students can choose to apply which uni and change their minds), UCAS guidance provided within college.
- STEP and AEA exams available especially for Oxbridge Maths applicants
- Free Aspire tests
- 47 GCSEs subjects available (66% got A* to B grades)
Host Families:
- All from local areas
- School directly in charge of and responsible for host arrangement and selection (not outsourced)
- High satisfaction rate from students (>85%)
- 2 meals (breakfast and dinner) provided during weekdays. Recommend students to bring GBP 5 for lunch.
- 3 meals provided on holidays
- Rates/price depends on commuting time (NOT distances)
- Price range: GBP 6,600-7,500 (Price INCLUDES travel pass)
- Accommodation on first-come-first-serve basis
- No extra guardian required for students"|"MURPHY Melissa"|""|""
